This PR reads the public dir recursively on server start and keeps an in-memory set of all public files so we can avoid going through sirv.

later.title: time: rename `cached_when` to `registered_when`
later.description:
What?
This PR renames the TimerShared::cached_when to TImerShared::registered_when to make the name more self-describing.
Why?
The word cache usually hints loading something is expensive, so the cached_when is likely making developer think this field cached the StateCell::state as loading it is expensive.
But actually,


The cached_when is only for locating the TimerEntry in the intrusive linked list.
The StateCell::state is the single source of truth while picking the expired TimerEntrys.
Loading the StateCell:state is also an relaxed load, which is the same operation as loading the cached_when, and it not more expensive than loading cached_when.

So the better name of cached_when is regist

later.title: BUGFIX: Mark the rule's restoration process as completed always

An alert being restored is used as a proxy for "we're now ready to write ALERTS/ALERTS_FOR_SERIES metrics" so as a result we weren't writing the series if we didn't restore anything the first time around

Previously it was possible to route to fallible services by either passing one directly to route("/", some_fallible_service) or applying a fallible middleware. So we recommended always using handle_error to convert errors into responses.
I think a simpler model would be to always require all services to be infallible. This means you can longer route to fallible services but I think thats a very niche feature that is fine to drop support for.

This PR introduces a graph-based execution model into the terraform test framework. With this model, test runs are able to execute in parallel. later.title: Terraform test: Consolidate test execution procedure
later.description:
This pull request consolidates the full test execution procedure into a single package, where the .Execute function is responsible for executing the run. The plan and apply command stages are separated into testPlan and testApply. In this code, we have only one waiter along the lifetime of the execute function. The waiter can be updated with a new terraform context at any time. This is typically done before a terraform operation.
Additionally, this PR introduces the concept of cleanup nodes into the graph. These nodes are responsible for cleaning up the state after test runs. In the future, we could make cleanup nodes run in parallel to optimize the cleanup process.

later.title: instances: "skipUnregistered" instead of "skipUnknown" internally
later.description:
Recently (in #34289) we've introduced the idea of the expansion of a particular module or resource not yet being known, which has inadvertently introduced some ambiguity about what "unknown" means in this package: "unknown" previously represented "not registered yet", which is different than having explicitly registered that we don't know.
To remove that ambiguity, we'll now use the term "unregistered" to talk about the "not registered yet" situation, and reserve "unknown" for when we know that we definitely don't know.
This is only an internal naming change within the package and doesn't affect any exported API.
